technique: One complete transparent painting per side. Only transparent-margin cropping and a uniform reduction are applied to the selected master.

N.prompt: Create one finished native-alpha 2D game sprite. Reference 1 is the art direction, material palette and inventory of the COMPLETE treasure reserve; repaint that whole hoard from the requested viewpoint as a single illustration. Reference 2 gives the precise chest facing and fittings only. This is an indivisible landscape-format game painting of a hoard for a dark isometric dungeon, not a sheet of parts. The two chests, five leather purses and a large three-dimensional mound of little gold coins grow together into one connected irregular mass; nestle objects deep in treasure, coins partly on the sacks’ feet and against chest bases, a bag leans into wood, coherent upper-left cool highlights, reflected warm gold bounce and joined dark contact shadows. Keep the original dark plum wooden planks, heavy chamfered blue-steel braces/horned corners and violet detail, oxblood leather purple ties and restrained plain honey-gold coins. One larger visibly OPEN chest with raised lid, one smaller CLOSED chest, three tied bags and two open purses. Objects must have the same silhouettes and scale across the four views; large chest about a quarter of total width; mound about as high as closed chest, bags to lower edges. Fixed orthographic 2:1 game isometry, ground axes slope ±1/2, upright verticals, camera 30° above ground, no vanishing point. The entire hoard fits inside a 2x2 diamond room; keep a compact obliquely oriented footprint, no linear display of props. Preserve chunky legible shapes, small elliptical coins, grouped strokes and shared ink, no photoreal or grain. Paint all visible occlusion and local shadows together. Transparent empty exterior, fully uncropped with a clear safety margin on every side. Absolutely no flagstones, platform, walls, backdrop, drop shadow rectangle, torches, text, labels, arrows or effects. ONE group and one camera angle only. The entrance is diagonally UPPER RIGHT on the screen. Both chests are opening AWAY from the viewer toward that upper-right corner; paint their BACKS, two rear hinges on uninterrupted plum rear panels, violet locks are on the unseen side. Reference 2 is the exact camera aspect of the chest rear. The open larger chest is on screen RIGHT of the small closed chest, both on the upper-right side of the composition. The high dense bank of gold is in the opposite LOWER LEFT, foreground, spilling into the feet of the chests. The cluster recedes diagonally from the lower left to upper right. Do not let the foreground bank conceal either chest lid.
